chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Hamzah, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'To enter the market with me having dirhams to buy meat with it for my dependents, and they have desired it, is more beloved to me than if I were to emancipate a person.'
ai.seo_question: Why is providing for family through trade considered superior to freeing a slave in this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) prioritizes the active provision of sustenance and satisfaction of family desires through lawful trade over the singular act of manumitting a slave, emphasizing the continuous virtue of self-sufficiency. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that earning a living to care for dependents is a sustained act of worship that prevents reliance on others, thereby preserving dignity and reducing social burden.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Hama who said,

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If I<sup>asws</sup> were to enter the market and with me<sup>asws</sup> was one Dirham to buy meat with it for my<sup>asws</sup> dependants and they had desired it, it would be more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than if I<sup>asws</sup> were to emancipate (liberate) a person’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from abu Hamzah who has said the following:
“Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘I love going to the market to buy meat for my family who strongly desire it, more than setting free an enslaved soul.’”
